  "title": "UK MPs Deny Vote Undermines Animal Sentience Recognition",
  "content": "MPs have been forced to deny that a recent Commons vote means animals are no longer recognized as sentient life forms in the UK. The controversy stems from a defeated amendment to the European Union (Withdrawal) Bill, which aimed to transfer the EU protocol on animal sentience into UK law. The vote, which took place on 15 November, saw the amendment rejected by 313 votes to 295, sparking a heated debate over its implications.\n\nTory MP Zac Goldsmith took to Twitter to clarify the situation, calling some of the reporting on the vote 'weird and dishonest.' He emphasized that the vote was about the legal procedure for ensuring animal welfare standards, not the principle of animal sentience. Fellow Conservative Rachel Maclean, MP for Redditch, also addressed the confusion in a video, labeling it as 'fake news' and reaffirming the government's commitment to protecting animals as sentient beings. She stated, 'This government, and in fact all governments, are deeply committed to continuing to protect animals as sentient beings. That law is already written into our own law.'\n\nPrime Minister Theresa May echoed these sentiments during Wednesday’s Prime Minister’s Questions, asserting, 'We recognize and respect that animals are sentient beings, and should be treated accordingly.' Tory MP Hugo Swire shared a letter from Environment Secretary Michael Gove on social media, reinforcing the message that MPs do not dispute the sentience of animals. Swire added, 'I do not believe that any MP thinks that animals do not have feelings or emotions.'\n\nDespite these assurances, the vote has triggered protests from animal rights groups, with multiple online petitions targeting the House of Lords, UK Parliament, and Michael Gove. Public figures, including presenter Sue Perkins, have also criticized MPs over the issue. Gudrun Ravetz, senior vice-president of the British Veterinary Association, expressed concern over the vote, stating, 'It is extremely concerning that a marginal majority of MPs have voted down this seminal clause. This action undermines the government’s previous promises that the UK will continue to be known for our high standards of animal health and welfare post-Brexit.'\n\nHowever, Conservative MP Henry Smith pointed out that EU law still permits many practices opposed by animal rights groups. The amendment, proposed by Green Party co-leader Caroline Lucas and others, sought to incorporate Article 13 of Title II of the Lisbon Treaty into UK law. During the debate, Lucas highlighted that the clause originated during the 1997 UK presidency of the EU and that since 1999, EU law has explicitly recognized animals as sentient life forms.\n\nThe debate continues as animal welfare advocates push for stronger protections, while MPs insist that the vote was procedural and does not reflect a change in the UK's stance on animal sentience.",
  "source": "The Guardian",
  "tags": ["UK Politics", "Animal Rights", "Brexit", "Sentience", "Parliament"]
}
